voiceover: You can only write the report if your roommate is also on their laptop. That is not a coincidence. ADHD brains run on an interest-based nervous system — dopamine is low at baseline, so starting a task alone feels impossible. But add one other person doing their own thing nearby, and your brain borrows their nervous system energy to regulate itself. No instructions needed. No talking. Just a warm body in the room. Virtual co-working calls do the same thing. Find a body double before you need to start — not after you have already been staring at the blank doc for 40 minutes. Follow for daily ADHD content.

title: Why You Only Focus When Someone Else Is There #Shorts
description: If you can only get things done when someone else is in the room, your ADHD brain is not broken — it is borrowing dopamine regulation from their nervous system. Body doubling is a science-backed focus hack that works with your brain chemistry, not against it. Learn why it works and how to use it even when you are alone.

voiceover: Your brain won't start the task. So bribe it. A dopamine menu is a short list of small rewards your brain actually likes — not 'healthy treats', real ones. Before you open that thing you've been avoiding, you pick one item off the menu. Maybe it's a specific playlist, a good drink, a candle, five minutes outside. You're not rewarding yourself after — you're front-loading the dopamine so your brain has a reason to launch. Write three to five items tonight. Keep the list visible. Then next time you can't start, you don't negotiate — you just pick. Follow for daily ADHD content.
